title: Free DISC personality test: find your DISC style — cv.cm
description: Free DISC personality test: rate 20 statements to see whether your style is Dominance, Influence, Steadiness or Conscientiousness, with a score for each. No sign-up; answers stay in your browser.
lede: Are you direct, outgoing, steady or precise? Rate 20 statements to find your main DISC style, how strong the other three are, and how you tend to work with people.
about: DISC describes four styles of behavior: Dominance (direct, results first), Influence (outgoing, persuasive), Steadiness (patient, supportive) and Conscientiousness (accurate, careful). The model goes back to the psychologist William Moulton Marston, who described four patterns of emotion and behavior in his 1928 book Emotions of Normal People. Others later turned his ideas into workplace questionnaires.

The statements here were written for cv.cm. This is not Everything DiSC or any other commercial assessment and has no link to their publishers; DiSC is a registered trademark of its owner. DISC is widely used in training but is less well supported by research than the Big Five, so use your result to start a conversation, not to make hiring decisions.

faq.q: What do the four DISC letters stand for?
faq.a: D is Dominance, I is Influence, S is Steadiness and C is Conscientiousness. Some versions use slightly different words, but the four styles are much the same.

faq.q: How is the DISC result worked out?
faq.a: Each style has five statements, scored 0 to 4. Your result is the style with the highest score, and the bars show all four. If two styles tie, the page names both.
None. D gets things moving, I brings people along, S keeps a team steady and C keeps the quality high. Good teams need all four, and most people use more than one.

faq.q: Is this the official DiSC assessment?
faq.a: No. It is a free, independent test based on the same public idea. Commercial reports are longer and have their own scoring, so your result there may differ.

items: I say what I want and go after it directly.
I find it easy to start a conversation with almost anyone.
I'm patient, even when things take a long time.
I check the details before I call something finished.
I like making the final call when a decision is needed.
I enjoy getting people excited about an idea.
I prefer a steady pace to sudden changes.
I follow the rules and procedures because they usually exist for a reason.
A tough challenge makes me want to try harder.
People often tell me I'm fun to be around.
I'd rather help the team succeed than stand out myself.
I want the facts and evidence before I make up my mind.
I care more about results than about keeping everyone comfortable.
I'm usually optimistic, even when plans go wrong.
I'm a good listener, and people come to me when they need support.
I hold myself to high standards of accuracy.
I get impatient when people take too long to act.
I would rather talk something through than write it down.
I stay loyal to the people and places I know.
I like to plan carefully and think through what could go wrong.

D.name: Dominance (D)
D.body: You are direct, decisive and driven by results. You like a challenge and move fast when others hesitate. Watch for coming across as blunt: slowing down to listen will win you more support.

I.name: Influence (I)
I.body: You are outgoing, warm and persuasive. You bring energy to a group and get people on board. Watch for losing track of details or promising too much: a short written plan helps.

S.name: Steadiness (S)
S.body: You are patient, dependable and supportive. People trust you and teams feel calmer with you around. Watch for avoiding conflict or sudden change: saying what you need early helps everyone.

C.name: Conscientiousness (C)
C.body: You are careful, analytical and precise. You want to get things right and you back your views with evidence. Watch for over-analyzing or being too critical: sometimes good enough, on time, is the better choice.
